newsitem.title: URUGUAY: Armed men beat, threaten Iran official in Uruguay.
newsitem.headline: Armed men beat, threaten Iran official in Uruguay.

text.p: Two masked men armed with revolvers forced their way into Iran's embassy in Uruguay where they beat an official and threatened to detonate explosives before escaping, the Iranian ambassador said on Friday.
"They wanted to kill me and then blow up the embassy," Ambassador Mohamed Ali Sarnadi told Reuters.
"Nobody but the Zionists could do something like this," Sarnadi said, "But the Uruguayan authorities will have to confirm that."
He added, "Uruguay is a quiet country, where we don't have any problems."
The men entered the embassy in Montevideo carrying bundles they said contained explosives. They beat an Iranian official and escaped soon after.
Uruguay is just across the River Plate from Argentina's capital Buenos Aires, which was the scene of bloody anti-Jewish bombings in 1992 and 1994.
Israel and the United States blamed Iranian-backed guerrillas for the attacks, although Iran denied this.
